# Results — Study 270 (Underwear-Index) on the NBER calendar + Shiller S&P 500

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The men's-underwear index
and the NBER recession calendar are hardcoded in [`data.py`](../underwear_index/data.py)
(1992–2024). **The underwear series is a curated reconstruction, not an audited dataset**
(see [`docs/references.md`](references.md)). S&P 500 calendar-year price returns are from
the Shiller monthly dataset (`_cache/shiller_sp500.parquet`). Match the fingerprint below
to confirm you hold the same data. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | n | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shiller S&P 500 (nominal price, Dec/Dec) | 1992–2024 | 33 years | `a59af6e1883f` |
| Underwear index (reconstructed) | 1992–2024 | 33 years, **4 dips** | hardcoded constant |
| NBER recession years | 2001, 2007, 2008, 2009, 2020 | 5 years | hardcoded constant |

Dip years (underwear YoY < 0): **2001, 2008, 2009, 2020**.

## The base rate — the key number

A year is followed by an NBER recession in **5 of 33** cases → the unconditional
next-year recession rate is **15.2%**. This is the correct null for any "trouble is
coming" flag. Recessions are rare, so a default forecast of "no recession" is right
most of the time and the bar for adding value is high.

## Leading-indicator view (dip in year Y → recession in year Y+1) — the genuine claim

| Arm | n | next-year recession rate |
|---|--:|--:|
| After a DIP (signal: trouble) | 4 | **25.0%** (1 of 4) |
| After NO dip | 29 | **13.8%** (4 of 29) |
| Unconditional | 33 | 15.2% |

2×2 table (dip × next-year recession): `a=1, b=3, c=4, d=25`.

- **Fisher exact p (one-sided): 0.4996** — not significant.
- **Permutation p (10,000 shuffles of dip labels): 0.4941** — the observed +11pp
  excess sits squarely inside the null distribution.
- The +11pp lift rests on a single dip-then-recession case (2008→2009). With only
  4 dips this is indistinguishable from chance.

## Coincident view (same year) — TAUTOLOGICAL, reported only as a control

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| Recession rate in dip years | 100.0% |
| Fisher exact p | 0.0001 |
| Permutation p | 0.0000 |

This p < 0.001 is **not a finding**: the reconstructed index has its dips drawn *on*
recession years, so "a dip means a recession this year" is circular by construction.
It is included only to show that one year of forbidden look-ahead is the entire
difference between "highly significant" and "null".

## Could you trade it? (dip → flat next year, no look-ahead, 10 bps one-way)

| metric | value |
|---|--:|
| Buy & hold S&P (price-only) | **8.6%/yr** |
| Underwear timing (gross) | 7.4%/yr |
| Underwear timing (net of 10 bps) | **7.4%/yr** |
| Turnover (avg position change/yr) | 0.22 |
| HAC (Newey-West) t on the spread | **−0.94** |

The timing rule **loses** to buy-and-hold: it goes flat the year after a dip and so
sits out the post-recession rebounds (2009 +27%, 2021 +27% followed dip years). The
spread's HAC t is negative — there is no edge, and the shortfall is structural
(missed rebounds), not a cost artifact (it persists at 0 bps).

## The n = 33 / 4-dip problem

With 4 dip years and a 15.2% base recession rate, the standard error on the
dip-conditional recession rate is √(0.152·0.848/4) ≈ **±18pp**. To clear Fisher
p < 0.05 you would need roughly 3–4 of the 4 dips followed by a recession — an effect
so large it would be self-evident. We observe **1 of 4**. The test is powerless at
this sample size; no honest claim survives.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** As a *leading* indicator the dip is noise: Fisher p = 0.50,
  perm p = 0.49, on only 4 dips. The coincident "significance" is a construction
  tautology, not evidence. (Survivorship is not a concern — single index, price-only.)
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The only implementable rule (dip → cash) earns 7.4%/yr
  net vs 8.6%/yr buy-and-hold; HAC t = −0.94. No vehicle, negative edge.
- **Busted — a story, not a forecast.** The famous 2008 dip was coincident with the
  slump, not ahead of it; n = 33 with 4 dips cannot resolve any effect.
